findings.title: Freeze and judge the actual launched weapon cohort
findings.detail: take() admits births from every later natural-war frame into case_ordinals; the judge then accepts the first terminal row without checking its weapon identity, required fields, matched launch selection or zero pending count. A later unrelated weapon can therefore supply the claimed changed result; completed only means no exception, including a settle deadline with pending case weapons. Empty/missing terminal fields are converted to empty strings rather than refused. This undermines the new launch-through-glue authority claim, not the measured finite ground-query conformance.
findings.requested_change: Freeze immediate post-launch births once; accept exactly one terminal per cohort member and no foreign/missing IDs; require complete matched launch/config and terminal evidence, correct cardinalities and all healthy case members ended. Add meaningful later-birth/foreign-terminal/missing-field/incomplete-cohort controls without inventing physics.

findings.title: Judge the accepted single-precision reply rather than the provider double
findings.detail: The witness formats the provider Lua double before the bridge nearest_f32 conversion, then compares that text with the C weapon terminal single. Adding 37.5 is not guaranteed to produce an exact f32: 255.99998474121094 + 37.5 is 293.49998474121094, between the adjacent singles. Valid provider replies can therefore fail the claimed exact receipt/outcome relation even when correctly consumed. No actual native authority result is claimed here.
findings.requested_change: Use a deliberately f32-exact changed witness point, or record the exact consumed single values at the boundary. Retain exact comparison and test a nonrepresentable-double receipt; do not add tolerances, round artifacts or alter original physical oracles.

findings.title: Preserve complete caller FP state in the newly exposed above entry
findings.detail: The new host_terrain_ground_above wrapper invokes ground_begin(fegetenv; fesetround toward-zero) and restores only fesetenv. The retained actual MinGW12-posix toolchain control demonstrates this exact sequence restores x87 but leaves MXCSR rounding at toward-zero for callers initially in the other three modes. Furthermore finite validation precedes the snapshot and can raise flags on nonfinite inputs. This is a new public-entry caller-state defect, not a claimed ground-fold mismatch; all three finite physical comparisons passed. Closed below/impact numerical algorithms are not reopened.
findings.requested_change: Use a complete caller-state guard around the new exposed entry, including early refusal paths; shared guard reuse is appropriate without changing original internal rounding/math. Verify success and refusal across all four caller rounding modes with nonzero status flags and exact x87 control/status plus MXCSR restoration. Preserve reference-world compatibility; do not introduce a host rounding workaround as proof.

findings.title: Make the new authority witness finite and propagate output failures
findings.detail: The simulated deadline loop has no monotonic-clock check or finite frame-count bound. A stalled clock loops forever, while the Rust parent blocks in Command::output without a wall deadline. The new writer also ignores write/flush/close results, including closing after its success evidence. Its declared bounded/retained-evidence contract is not enforced on these failure paths.
findings.requested_change: Enforce finite positive progress/frame budgets and a bounded child wait; fail on every output write/flush/close error. Cover a stalled clock and actual driver writer-error collaborators. Preserve ordinary simulation/query order and never treat missing evidence as an expected refusal.

findings.title: Restore the required strict all-target lint gate
findings.detail: The actual unchanged Linux build finishes 441 passing test functions, then exits101 on thirteen new indexing_slicing errors in these helpers. The bounded callsites do not establish a memory-corruption finding; this is a concrete required validation failure, not a passed check.
findings.requested_change: Destructure fixed-size arrays or use checked slice/array conversions for the numeric helpers without suppressing the lint or weakening validation; rerun the affected strict checks and retain the original failure.
